root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the first bridge-address slot becomes bridge-owned cleanup state, `config__read_file_core()` must duplicate `token` into `cur_bridge->addresses[cur_bridge->address_count-1].address` instead of storing the raw line-buffer alias directly.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original appends the first parsed bridge address by storing the in-place `strtok_r` token pointer itself, so later error unwinding can leave bridge cleanup owning a pointer into the reusable line buffer. The fixed original duplicates the token at the append site, so the same first-slot store no longer aliases the parser buffer.

nodes.state: `config__bridge_cleanup()` forwards the stale first bridge-address pointer into `mosquitto__FREE()` as the AddressSanitizer-reported bad-free sink.

When `config__read_file()` unwinds after the invalid-port error, `mosquitto__FREE(buf)` ends the shared line-buffer lifetime while the first stored bridge-address field still holds that same aliased pointer.

edges.relation: The first stored bridge-address pointer remains unchanged when control returns to `config__read_file()`, so the caller still holds the raw token alias in bridge state at the moment it frees the shared line buffer.
After `config__read_file()` frees the shared line buffer, later bridge cleanup reaches `mosquitto__FREE(bridge->addresses[i].address)` with that same stale first-address pointer.

The invalid-port return from the first parsed bridge address is the exact error code observed by `config__read_file()` as it unwinds into `mosquitto__FREE(buf)`, which is why the later `mosquitto__strdup()` repair never runs on this path.
